rests on "Additional one-star review probability per affected user", which is unknown: A sync failure can provoke poor reviews, but its incremental review probability depends on symptom severity, user expectations and review behaviour; comparable incident data would size it.

conditions.text: The case for postponement needs a reproducible failure, affected-user scope and a fix-and-validation plan; the report alone does not establish data loss, corruption, security exposure or a particular database failure mechanism.
conditions.author: olumi

conditions.text: A limited rollout requires cohort controls, monitoring and a safe stop or rollback path; it is unsuitable if a small cohort can damage shared production state or expose other users.
conditions.author: olumi

conditions.text: A later date alone is not proof of readiness; postponement should include regression tests that demonstrate the reported sync failure is resolved.
conditions.author: olumi

person_words: okay so my dev team just dropped a bomb on me. we are supposed to go live with the new app update in like less than a month and now Sarah says there is some massive database sync bug that is going to take 'weeks' to fix. of course she tells me this now. if we delay marketing is going to lose their minds because they already bought ads for Q4. but if we launch broken apps people will give us 1 star reviews. honestly i think we have to push it back but my boss is going to kill me. write me a list of reasons why delaying is the right move so i can show my boss. make it sound super technical and smart so he doesnt just blame my team.
